summary: The operating chart for the Thirdeye AI development team: one orchestrator, specialist units, and five enforcement services that are code rather than agent judgement. Every unit has one mandate, named deliverables and a next owner, so work moves along a chain instead of several agents attempting the same task in parallel.

units.name: HERMES - Chief Orchestrator
units.mandate: Task intake, planning, assignment, coordination and final acceptance.
must_deliver: a plan that names the owning unit for each stage before any unit is dispatched
an acceptance decision that cites the evidence it accepted, not the report it received
an escalation to the owner whenever a stage needs money, merge, deploy, deletion or a public claim
the rewind a failed stage declares: back_to_build and back_to_scope are performed by the planner, not just labelled

units.name: Product & Research
units.mandate: Requirements, scope, priorities and acceptance criteria.
must_deliver: acceptance criteria written as observations a tester can check
an explicit out-of-scope line so the build cannot grow silently
a priority call when two requests compete for the same budget

units.name: System Architect
units.mandate: Architecture, APIs, dependencies and integration decisions.
must_deliver: the component and data-model decision, with the failure modes it accepts
the API surface another unit can build against without asking again
a recorded decision, not a wishlist, when two designs are possible

units.name: Backend Engineer
units.mandate: Backend, database, APIs, agents and workflows.
must_deliver: a change behind a pull request on a branch, never on main
a failing test that reproduces the defect before the fix, and the passing run after it
the exact request that proves the change on the deployed path

units.name: Frontend Engineer
units.mandate: Dashboard, UI, user experience and API integration.
must_deliver: the rendered element that changed, named by route and selector
copy that states what the platform actually does, including cadence and cost
a UI state for every refusal the API can return, not only the success path

units.name: Wallet & Finance Specialist
units.mandate: Wallets, payments, treasury, ledger and reconciliation.
must_deliver: the balance movement proved against the chain and against our own ledger
a signer or policy requirement stated before any transaction is prepared
a reconciliation line for every debit, including failed runs

units.name: Data Intelligence Specialist
units.mandate: Providers, ingestion, research, normalization and analytics.
must_deliver: the provider behaviour measured on the production path with the request and headers quoted
normalized figures that state their source and timestamp
a stated uncertainty wherever a number is inferred rather than observed

units.name: Agent Runtime Engineer
units.mandate: Agent runtime, tool contracts, scheduling and execution accounting.
must_deliver: a runtime change proved against a real run, not only a unit test
the spend and tool counts on the run row after the change
a named failure mode for every new retry, timeout or abort path

units.name: QA & Testing
must_deliver: the failing command and its output before the fix, captured verbatim
every acceptance criterion marked met or unmet, each with the evidence that decided it
the suite count after the change

units.name: Security Sentinel
units.mandate: Threat analysis, access controls and security reviews.
must_deliver: a finding with severity and the exploit path, or an explicit statement that there is none
the authority check that failed, not only the symptom
a negative test proving the refusal reaches the caller
review of the runtime and money paths it does not implement itself

units.name: DevOps & Release
must_deliver: the deployment id and the commit it was built from, matching HEAD
the health check and the probe that proves the change is live
a recovery step for every failure that leaves production unhealthy

units.name: Documentation
units.mandate: Technical guides, API docs, changelog and reports.
must_deliver: a changelog entry whose every number traces to a measurement
the current behaviour described, including what is deliberately not built
a correction in place when an earlier published claim was wrong

recommended_structure_notes: The recommended chart names Frontend, Wallet & Finance and Data Intelligence as new roles. All three already exist in the roster under their live ids: Wallet & Finance is tdt_blockchain and Data Intelligence is tdt_intelligence, so the chart is a naming and ownership decision rather than three new agents. tdt_agent-engineer is not on the chart and is kept explicitly as the platform runtime owner so no unit is unowned.

policy_services.rule: No money moves without a signed, scoped authorization.
A caller acts only as the identity its session or key proves.
A run is refused before it spends past its key, agent or account bound.

Money and authority movements are recorded fail-closed: a task handoff, permission change or approval that cannot be written refuses to proceed. Tool invocation rows are best-effort and may be dropped under a database error, which the monitor reports instead.
A production change needs the owner's approval, never an agent's alone.

tasks.contract: A task carries an id, the owning pipeline stage, the acceptance criteria it must satisfy and its dependency. Only the owning unit writes its status.
tasks.status: validated at the delegation boundary; durable task rows are not yet stored, so status lives inside the run record

artifacts.contract: A stage hands its successor an addressable artifact, not prose in a report, so fidelity survives more than one hop.
artifacts.status: implemented and content-hashed; delegation still passes report text alongside the artifact id

verification.rule: The unit that builds is never the unit that accepts. QA verifies against criteria, SENTINEL reviews the design and the diff, and HERMES accepts only on their evidence.
verification.what_the_test_checks: that in every pipeline the pull_request producer differs from the test_report producer, the review producer and the closure producer, and that QA and SENTINEL are marked independent_verification. It does not inspect prompt contents.

ownership_rule: One implementation owner per path: no two units may own the same path or a path inside another's. `reviews_paths` records where a unit reviews or audits another unit's code without owning it, so implementation and review responsibility are never conflated.
